html:
Two times a year, your phone explodes.

First heat wave of summer? Everyone's AC is dying. First cold snap of fall? Every furnace in town decides it's done. You're turning down calls. Your crew is exhausted. You're printing money.

Then the mild weather hits.

Suddenly it's 72 degrees outside and nobody needs anything. The calendar clears out. You're refreshing your voicemail hoping something breaks somewhere.

If you run an HVAC company, you already know this cycle by heart. The question is whether you're going to keep riding it or finally do something about it.

Spoiler: you can do something about it. And it's not as complicated as you think.

Why HVAC Companies Live and Die by the Weather (And How to Stop)

The honest truth is that most HVAC companies are great at doing the work and not so great at marketing when work isn't urgently needed.

During the busy season, there's no time. You're dispatching, quoting, fixing equipment, and barely keeping up. Marketing feels like something you'll figure out later.

Later comes. And nothing's in place.

Forbes Agency Council's breakdown of HVAC marketing strategies makes a point that hits close to home for most HVAC owners: the companies that stay consistently busy aren't necessarily better at the work. They're better at staying visible when customers aren't in emergency mode.

The goal isn't to make people need HVAC service in April. The goal is to make sure that when they do need it, yours is the only name they think of.

Six Ways to Keep the Calendar Full All Year

Sell Maintenance Plans Like They're Your Best Product

Because they are.

A maintenance plan is simple. The customer pays a set amount per year, you come out twice to tune up their system, and they get priority service if something breaks. For the customer, it's peace of mind. For you, it's guaranteed recurring revenue that doesn't depend on weather or emergencies.

Maintenance plans are the single best way to smooth out HVAC seasonality. They give you jobs to run in the slow months. They keep your name in front of customers regularly. And they make customers far more likely to call you when something bigger goes wrong, because you're already their HVAC company.

If you're not offering maintenance plans yet, start now. Price them so they're easy to say yes to and still worth your time.

Make Google Work for You Before the Rush

When a homeowner's AC quits at 6 p.m. on a Tuesday in July, they're not scrolling through a list of options. They're calling the first result that comes up on Google Maps.

Your Google Business Profile is what gets you there. A complete profile with current photos, accurate hours, a clear list of services, and consistent new reviews tells Google you're a real, active, trustworthy business. Google rewards that with better placement in local search results.

The trick is keeping it updated all year, not just when you're busy. Post a tip about changing air filters. Add a photo of a recent installation. Ask for a review after every job. None of this takes more than a few minutes, but it keeps your profile looking alive and active even in January.

Follow Up With Past Customers Before They Forget You

You serviced someone's system last summer. The job went great. They were happy. And then they never heard from you again.

Now it's spring. Their neighbor is asking around for a good HVAC company. Your past customer can't quite remember your name. So they just say "I don't know, Google someone."

A simple check-in email or text a few months after a service call fixes that. Something like "Hey, just a reminder that spring is a great time to get your AC tuned up before the heat hits. We'd love to help." Short. Friendly. Timely.

You don't need to write a novel. You just need to show up in their inbox before the competitor does.

Let Automation Handle the Follow-Through

Here's the honest part: you're not going to remember to send that email. Not manually. Not consistently. Not while you're also running a crew and answering emergency calls.

That's what automation is for. Set up a message that goes out automatically 90 days after a service call. Set up a seasonal reminder every spring and fall. Set up a review request that fires the day after every job closes. You build it once. It runs forever. Forbes Agency Council's piece on how home service contractors can use AI to beat the competition points out that automated follow-up is one of the fastest ways HVAC companies can close the gap on larger competitors without adding more people to the payroll.

Consistent follow-through wins jobs. Automation makes consistent follow-through actually possible.

Build Your Reputation While the Work Is Flowing

Every job you complete is a chance to get a review. Most HVAC companies get reviews occasionally, by accident, when a particularly happy customer decides to write one on their own.

That's not a strategy.

Ask every customer. Send a text right after you wrap up the job with a direct link to your Google review page. Most happy customers will do it if you make it easy and ask at the right time. A new review every week adds up fast. And a profile that shows consistent, recent reviews outranks a profile with more total reviews that stopped coming in two years ago.

Get Your Website Doing Something

A lot of HVAC companies have a website that looks fine but does nothing. It doesn't show up in search. It doesn't capture leads. It doesn't tell visitors what to do next.

Your website should be generating estimate requests around the clock. It should load fast on a phone. It should clearly show what you do, where you serve, and how to contact you. And it should include pages built around the terms people actually search for, things like "AC repair near me" or "furnace tune-up in [your city]."

A website that ranks and converts is one of the best investments you can make. It works while you're on a job, while you're asleep, and while you're dealing with everything else on your plate.

You Don't Have to Do All of This by Hand

Reading through this list, you might be thinking: there's no way I have time for all of that.

You're right. Not manually.

But that's exactly the point. The contractors who stay booked year-round aren't superheroes with more hours in the day. They have systems. And the right partner helps them build those systems without adding a second job to their plate.
